ambiguities_declared: The controlled relation vocabulary (has-mcl, has-mclg, has-mrdl, has-mrdlg, requires-monitoring, requires-treatment-technique) is designed for contaminant-specific numeric standards and does not map cleanly onto this section's procedural/administrative notice-content requirements; only 'applies-to' and 'defined-as' were used, and several requirements (e.g., the full ten-element list, presentation rules, distribution-encouragement language) were left as quotes/page proposals rather than forced into claims.

Paragraph (d)(1) references health effects language 'specified in appendix B' corresponding to violations 'listed in appendix A to this subpart' — the actual appendix A/B content is not included in this provided section, so the specific per-contaminant standard language cannot be verified or extracted here.

challenge_questions.expected_answer: A description of the violation/situation and contaminant level(s); when it occurred; potential adverse health effects; the population at risk; whether alternative water supplies should be used; what actions consumers should take; what the system is doing to correct it; when compliance/resolution is expected; the owner/operator/designee's name, address, and phone number; and a statement encouraging distribution of the notice.
challenge_questions.question: What ten elements must a public water system include in a public notice for an NPDWR violation or public notification situation?

challenge_questions.expected_answer: The same ten elements required under paragraph (a) for NPDWR violations.
challenge_questions.question: If a public water system violates the conditions of its variance or exemption, which notice content elements apply?

challenge_questions.expected_answer: Include notice information in the appropriate language(s), or provide a telephone number or address where persons served can obtain a translated copy of the notice or request assistance in the appropriate language.
challenge_questions.question: What must a water system do if it serves a large proportion of non-English speaking consumers, as determined by the primacy agency?

challenge_questions.expected_answer: No. Notices must not contain overly technical language or very small print, must not be formatted to defeat the notice's purpose, and must not contain language that nullifies its purpose.
challenge_questions.question: Can a public notice be printed with very small print or overly technical language?

challenge_questions.expected_answer: "We are required to monitor your drinking water for specific contaminants on a regular basis. Results of regular monitoring are an indicator of whether or not your drinking water meets health standards. During [compliance period], we “did not monitor or test” or “did not complete all monitoring or testing” for [contaminant(s)], and therefore cannot be sure of the quality of your drinking water during that time."
challenge_questions.question: What standard language must be included in a notice about a missed or incomplete monitoring/testing requirement?

verified_quotes.exact_text: When a public water system violates a NPDWR or has a situation requiring public notification, each public notice must include the following elements:
(1) A description of the violation or situation, including the contaminant(s) of concern, and (as applicable) the contaminant level(s);
(5) Whether alternative water supplies should be used;
(6) What actions consumers should take, including when they should seek medical help, if known;
(9) The name, business address, and phone number of the water system owner, operator, or designee of the public water system as a source of additional information concerning the notice; and
(2) If a public water system violates the conditions of a variance or exemption, the public notice must contain the ten elements listed in paragraph (a) of this section.
(ii) Must not contain overly technical language or very small print;

For public water systems serving a large proportion of non-English speaking consumers, as determined by the primacy agency, the public notice must contain information in the appropriate language(s) regarding the importance of the notice or contain a telephone number or address where persons served may contact the water system to obtain a translated copy of the notice or to request assistance in the appropriate language.

Public water systems must include in each public notice the health effects language specified in appendix B to this subpart corresponding to each MCL, MRDL, and treatment technique violation listed in appendix A to this subpart, and for each violation of a condition of a variance or exemption.

We are required to monitor your drinking water for specific contaminants on a regular basis. Results of regular monitoring are an indicator of whether or not your drinking water meets health standards. During [compliance period], we “did not monitor or test” or “did not complete all monitoring or testing” for [contaminant(s)], and therefore cannot be sure of the quality of your drinking water during that time.

Please share this information with all the other people who drink this water, especially those who may not have received this notice directly (for example, people in apartments, nursing homes, schools, and businesses). You can do this by posting this notice in a public place or distributing copies by hand or mail.
